item.title: Van de Zandschulp reaches US Open quarter-finals for second time
item.description:
Van de Zandschulp reaches US Open quarter-finals for second time

September 8, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch number one tennis player Botic van de Zandschulp has reached the quarter-finals of the US Open after winning a five-hour marathon against Frenchman Arthur Gea.

The 30-year-old came back from two sets down to win the third and fourth sets on a tie-break before clinching the final set 6-4 in a match that swung back and forth.

Van de Zandschulp was warned by the umpire at one point for smashing a ball out of the stadium in frustration, but regained his composure as he wore down Gea, who only got into the tournament as a lucky loser.

“I’ve had some tough years, but since this year things have gone better,” he said afterwards. “I still need to let it sink in, but tomorrow I’ll probably wake up feeling good.”

Gea took the first set 6-3 after Van de Zandschulp failed to convert two break points at 3-3, while in the second set the Dutchman surrendered a 4-1 lead before losing the tie-break to love.

Van de Zandschulp was on the point of going out in straight sets when Gea served for the match in the third-set tie-break.

But the Dutchman won the point and went on to take the fourth set, also on a tie-break, before making the decisive break at 3-3 in the decider. He served out the match to wrap up the win in five hours, 13 minutes.

His reward is a daunting quarter-final against the top seed, Alexander Zverev, after the German beat Italy’s Luciano Darderi in straight sets. Zverev is aiming for his second Grand Slam title after winning the French Open in June and reaching the final of Wimbledon.

item.title: Nationwide 24-hour transport strike to go ahead as unions rally
item.description:
Nationwide 24-hour transport strike to go ahead as unions rally

September 8, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Thousands of public sector workers are expected to rally in The Hague on Tuesday against the cabinet’s social security cuts, a day before a 24-hour strike halts all trains, buses, trams and metros across the country.

Staff from councils, provinces, ministries, water boards and universities will march to the finance ministry behind a mock golden coach, a week before the real one carries the king on Prinsjesdag.

Union federation FNV said the coach carries a briefcase of alternative plans for the cabinet. Home care and nursing home staff are also taking part, and The Hague’s street cleaners are on strike.

“This cabinet keeps putting the bill on ordinary people,” FNV chairman Hans Spekman said in a statement. “The social safety net we have all paid into for years is being dismantled.”

No trains on Wednesday
The rally is the second of three days of action this week. Dockers in Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Zeeland walked out on Friday, and on Wednesday public transport stops for 24 hours.

NS is running no regular trains at all. The only exception is the airport sprinter between Amsterdam Centraal, Schiphol and Hoofddorp, which will run four times an hour.

International services, including Eurostar, ICE, Eurocity and the NightJet, will not run within the Netherlands, nor will the regional trains to Antwerp and Aachen. It is the first nationwide 24-hour public transport strike since May 2019, when unions walked out over the state pension age.

Back to normal on Thursday
NS expects to run its normal timetable on Thursday but is advising passengers to check the NS app shortly before departure. Its refund scheme for delays applies on strike days, although a separate allowance for alternative transport was scrapped earlier this year.

FNV called the strike in July as part of its campaign against plans to shorten unemployment benefit and cut payments for the long-term sick and disabled.

Social affairs minister Hans Vijlbrief has since dropped a plan to raise the state pension age faster in line with life expectancy, and the cabinet has scrapped part of the remaining cuts and delayed others, according to the Telegraaf. The unions say most of the savings are still on the table.

item.title: Gridlock around A28 after bridge closed for emergency repairs
item.description:
Gridlock around A28 after bridge closed for emergency repairs

September 8, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Traffic on one of the main east-to-west routes through the Netherlands ground to a standstill on Tuesday morning after a motorway bridge was closed for emergency repairs.

The A28 has been closed at Nijkerk since Monday afternoon, when the highways agency Rijkswaterstaat closed the Hardenbergerbrug in both directions.

The motoring organisation ANWB reported a 23km tailback on the diversionary route on the A1 at 8.30am on Monday and 4km on the A704. Traffic was also at a standstill through Nijkerk.

The bridge was due to be repaired in November, but during an inspection the agency found that large quantities of sand and gravel around the concrete supports had washed away.

“The pillars are unstable and we can’t guarantee people’s safety,” spokeswoman Marike Broos told NOS.

The cycle bridge beneath the road and the canal below have also been closed to traffic.

Rijkswaterstaat is carrying out emergency repairs to support the bridge with sand and gravel before the strengthening works start in November, but it is not known when the road will reopen.

item.title: Nijmegen streets sealed off over gunfire report after Overasselt
item.description:
Nijmegen streets sealed off over gunfire report after Overasselt

September 8, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Armed police sealed off several streets in eastern Nijmegen on Monday evening after residents reported hearing what sounded like automatic gunfire. It turned out to be a false alarm, a week after the deadly attack in nearby Overasselt.

Officers ordered people around the Hengstdalseweg to stay indoors and out of sight, a police helicopter came in and the DSI special intervention unit of heavily armed police was called in. Police later said they had found no evidence that any shots had actually been fired.

“We are extra alert to reports like this at the moment,” a spokesperson told regional broadcaster Omroep Gelderland. A spokesperson told news agency ANP that the scale of the response was linked to the attack in Overasselt, roughly 10 kilometres to the south, in which two police officers were hit.

Belgian arrest
Police said on Sunday that a 26-year-old Belgian national had been arrested in Amsterdam on Friday in connection with the attack, bringing the total number of arrests to 35. Two people released earlier remain suspects.

Specialist teams backed by riot police are continuing to search Overasselt and the surrounding area for evidence.

Previous convictions
Several of the men being held have previous convictions for firearms offences, kidnapping and fraud, the AD reported on Monday, citing the list of suspects brought before an examining magistrate on Friday. Police declined to comment on the report to broadcaster NOS.

One 23-year-old from Amsterdam was jailed for four years after firing on a house in Antwerp in 2022, the AD said. The intended target was a relative of kickboxer Jamal Ben Saddik, but the gunmen hit the wrong address.

A second Amsterdam man was given 15 months, six of them suspended, for kidnapping and robbing an elderly man at gunpoint in 2024. A third, aged 20, appeared in court over a shooting late that year and is suspected of firing the fatal shots in Overasselt, according to the paper. Prosecutors have not said who they believe pulled the trigger.

item.title: Phone subscriptions for internationals: What you need to know
item.description:
Partner content

Phone subscriptions for internationals: What you need to know

September 7, 2026

Whether you’ve just moved here or are looking to change your mobile phone provider, finding a phone subscription in the Netherlands can be a daunting task. So many advertisements! So many choices! So many requirements!

Sometimes, it seems as if you’re stuck in a Catch-22 situation: you need a BSN (Dutch social security number) to get a contract, but you often have to pay for it with a Dutch bank card. But to open a Dutch bank account, you will have to provide most banks with a BSN number (four banks in the Netherlands – ING, bunq, ABN Amro and Revolut – let you open an account without it, but you still have to provide them with a BSN number within 90 days).

To avoid this bureaucratic spiral, mobile service provider Simyo offers contracts without the usual required BSN number, giving you the option of moving beyond the prepaid plans most other companies offer to those without a BSN.

You can also use a foreign bank account to pay for your contract (although you must arrange that with customer service).

What’s the deal?

Simyo has been voted Best in Test by the independent Dutch consumer organization Consumentenbond for the second quarter of this year – its 38th time with that distinction.

Launched by telecom giant KPN some 20 years ago as an online-only mobile service provider, the budget Simyo uses KPN’s reliable 5G network, meaning you get excellent quality for a competitive price. (And if you have KPN internet and TV, you’ll get extra data at no charge.)

“Overall satisfaction with Simyo receives a 9.8 in the second quarter,” writes the Consumentenbond, which rates how satisfied customers are with their provider. Overall, Simyo got a rating of 8.2, “making it the Best in Test in during the second quarter of 2026.”

Specifically, says the Consumentenbond, “Customers report few outages regarding mobile internet and calling. They also experience few issues with slow connections. Administrative problems hardly occur. For example, about 1% reports a non-working SIM card, problems logging into the account, or an unjustified debit.”

Simyo’s mobile abonnement beat out Odido, Lebara and Vodafone/Ziggo, among others, in the consumer organization’s ratings.

À la carte pricing
Simyo offers both Sim Only and phone subscriptions that bear out its stellar quality to price ratio, with a Sim Only plan costing as little as €6,50 per month for the first year, increasing to €15 per month after 12 months. (And that includes Dutch taxes!)

For those looking for a subscription, plans offering 40 GB of data and 400 min/sms start for just €6,50 monthly (a temporary offer). You choose your plan à la carte, meaning you can decide how many minutes, gigabytes or months you’re looking for and the price will adjust automatically as you build your plan on Simyo’s website.

Buy a data cap
Don’t forget to take out the data cap for an additional €1 per month to save you from unexpected costs when your bundle runs out; your internet will then stop automatically when it reaches your limit.

Flexibility
Flexibility is another compelling reason to choose Simyo: monthly subscriptions allow you to adjust or cancel according to your needs and budget, doing away with those one- or two-year set contracts that lock you and your bank account in until they expire. That’s a huge advantage for internationals residing in the Netherlands for just a short period.

Data bundle
Simyo offers a data bundle for outside the EU that makes calling and internet surfing affordable while travelling.

eSIM cards
Simyo also offers eSIM (embedded SIM) cards that save you the hassle of inserting plastic chips, as you can download your mobile plan by scanning a code or using an app. You can manage your subscription via the user-friendly Mijn Simyo app.

“I wanted a second mobile number, for distant external contacts, to protect my main number,” wrote user Bert on Trustpilot, who gave Simyo a 5-star rating. “With an e-sim card from Simyo, I fixed that in 15 minutes, and it works fine.”

So if you’re looking for a new mobile phone plan, updating your old one or buying one for your teenage children, Simyo is an easy, affordable and reliable choice.

item.title: Netherlands must double water spending, delta commissioner warns
item.description:
Netherlands must double water spending, delta commissioner warns

September 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands must at least double what it spends on keeping the sea out and fresh water in, and even then it will not be able to prevent all the damage from climate change, delta commissioner Co Verdaas said on Monday.

Spending on flood defences, fresh water and climate-proofing currently amounts to about 1% of GDP, or just over €11 billion a year, and needs to rise to at least 2%, broadcaster NOS reported. His statements come ahead of the national budget day next week.

Verdaas gave a six-yearly review of the national delta programme to infrastructure minister Vincent Karremans. Carrying on as before “is not an option”, the infrastructure ministry said in a statement. The review stressed that the country is in “the next chapter of our water tradition.”

“We are world-renowned for our water management,” Verdaas said. “But this summer’s extremes have once again rubbed our noses in the facts. We are not going to make it with technology alone,” Verdaas said.

Pumps and salt
The review calls for billions of euros in new pumps at IJmuiden and, later, on the Afsluitdijk, so that river water can still be pushed out to sea as levels rise. NOS puts the IJmuiden works alone at around €2 billion. The pumping station protects some 4 million people, as well as Schiphol.

Preparations should also start now on new “Delta Works” to replace the Maeslantkering storm surge barrier near Rotterdam, and the IJsselmeer should be allowed to hold more water so it can keep supplying half the country in dry summers.

But technical fixes will not be enough, Verdaas said. Land use will have to change in the most vulnerable areas, including the bulb-growing Bollenstreek, the sandy soils of the east and south, the Noord-Holland coast and parts of Friesland and Groningen, where salt water is creeping in and farmers may have to change the crops they grow.

Households should expect “wet feet and flooded cellars” more often, the statement says, and hospitals and power installations will need extra protection from cloudbursts.

The findings follow a summer in which the Rhine fell to its lowest level in 80 years and the government formally declared a water shortage. The full Deltaprogramma 2027, with the revised strategy, is published on Prinsjesdag, September 15, alongside the budget.

item.title: Nazi’s daughter gives up looted Goudstikker painting
item.description:
Nazi’s daughter gives up looted Goudstikker painting

September 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The daughter of a Nazi official has given up all claim to a painting looted from the collection of Amsterdam art dealer Jacques Goudstikker, a year after it was spotted hanging above her sofa in photos on an Argentine estate agent’s website.

A federal judge in Mar del Plata approved a settlement on Friday in which Patricia Kadgien and her husband Juan Carlos Cortegoso can avoid trial for concealing the work, Argentinian media reported.

In return they have to each pay 2.4 million pesos, around €1,400, to a local mother and child hospital.

Portrait of a Lady now passes to Marei von Saher, Goudstikker’s daughter-in-law and sole heir, who has spent decades tracking down works from the collection. Her lawyers said she has agreed to let it go on show in Argentina before it is handed over, AP reported.

Estate agent’s photos
The painting had been missing since the war until August 2025, when AD journalists researching Kadgien’s father recognised it in photos of her house, which was for sale.

Friedrich Kadgien was financial adviser to Hermann Göring and fled to Argentina after the war. He died there in 1978 without ever being charged.

By the time police raided the house, the painting had gone and a tapestry of horses hung in its place. The couple were placed under house arrest and handed the work to prosecutors a week later.

Not a Ghislandi
The portrait of the Contessa Colleoni was catalogued by Goudstikker as the work of Giuseppe Ghislandi, but a court-ordered examination by Argentina’s national academy of fine arts concluded it was painted by Giacomo Ceruti, another 18th-century Italian, according to AP. Experts put its value at around $290,000.

Goudstikker died in May 1940 after falling into the hold of the ship carrying him away from the German invasion. Some 1,100 works from his stock were sold under duress to Göring and other senior Nazis, and the Dutch state returned 202 of them to his heirs in 2006.

item.title: Amsterdam canal swim raises record €3m for ALS research
item.description:
Amsterdam canal swim raises record €3m for ALS research

September 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

More than 3,300 people swam 2km through Amsterdam’s canals on Sunday and raised a record €3 million for research into the muscle-wasting disease ALS. Last year’s event brought in just under €1.73 million.

Swimmers set off from the Keizersgracht in groups every few minutes and finished at the Marineterrein, next to the maritime museum. A shorter 750-metre swim for children and less experienced swimmers took place earlier in the day.

Among the participants were 12 people who have ALS, some swimming under their own power and others towed through the water by family and friends. Television presenter Beau van Erven Dorens, radio host Marieke Elsinga, actress Monic Hendrickx and singer Maaike Ouboter also took part.

Hellespont origins
The event grew out of a 2011 fundraiser in which a group of friends swam the Hellespont in Turkey in memory of a friend who had died of ALS, raising €90,000.

The first Amsterdam edition followed in 2012, when some 1,100 swimmers, including the then Princess Máxima, raised €740,000.

ALS, or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, causes progressive loss of muscle control and has no cure. Most patients die within three to five years of their first symptoms. Around 500 people in the Netherlands are diagnosed every year, according to broadcaster NOS.

Donations remain open until the end of September and the final total will be announced on October 1.

item.title: Last taste of summer today before the rain sets in
item.description:
Last taste of summer today before the rain sets in

September 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Monday is set to be the last warm day for a while, with temperatures ranging from 24°C on the coast to as high as 29°C in Limburg and along the eastern border, according to the KNMI.

The weather service expects a fairly sunny afternoon with a brisk south-westerly wind, strong along the south-west coast. Cloud will build from the west in the evening, with a chance of a shower in places.

Change will come on Tuesday, when NOS weather forecasters expect highs of no more than 18°C or 19°C, lots of clouds and a lengthy spell of rain. Wednesday will also be cooler, with wind on both days.

Thursday should be drier, with temperatures around 20°C when the sun is out. Longer term, forecasters expect a mix of sunshine and showers at fairly average September temperatures, with no return of summer-like weather in sight.

Meteorological autumn began on 1 September.

item.title: Snapchat sued over addictive design in mass claim
item.description:
Snapchat sued over addictive design in mass claim

September 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A Dutch consumer foundation has filed a mass claim against the maker of Snapchat over the app’s “addictive” design, the second such case brought against the platform in the Netherlands in three months.

Consumer mass claims foundation SMC wants the court in Amsterdam to force Snap, Snapchat’s US parent company, to switch off features it says are built to keep users hooked unless a user deliberately turns them on.

It is also seeking compensation of between €425 and €1,850 per user, depending on how heavily and at what age they used the app.

In June, another foundation filed a similar case over Snapchat’s design and its use of personal data for advertising. A judge will decide which of the two can represent Dutch users.

Streaks and scores
Snapchat lets users send photos and messages that disappear after they’ve been viewed, and has more than 6 million monthly users in the Netherlands, who open the app around 40 times a day, according to figures cited by the foundation.

Features such as the “streak”, broken if two friends go a day without messaging, and the “snapscore”, which rises with use, pressure young people to keep coming back, SMC says. Internal Snap emails released in a US court case last year described the streak as “unintentionally addictive” and “fairly unhealthy”, the foundation said.

A Snap spokesperson told Algemeen Dagblad (AD) that the company remained committed to making Snapchat “a safe, positive and authentic place”, and that users valued streaks as a way to stay in touch. Snap said it had made it easy to pause and restore a streak, although restoring one costs €1 euro each time after a free first use.

SMC also wants Snapchat made safer for younger users, including curbs on location features it says allow strangers to find children, and action against accounts linked to drug dealing and grooming. Snap said location sharing on its map is off by default and that users have to choose to switch it on.

Under EU rules
The foundation argues the design breaches EU rules that require large platforms to protect users from addictive features. The European Commission has been investigating Snapchat over how it safeguards minors since 2025, and the Dutch consumer regulator (ACM) is examining the same question.

The case follows a US settlement last month in which Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion and overhaul Instagram and Facebook for minors, a deal that named Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube as platforms expected to follow.

The first hearing is expected in about three months. Snapchat users, and parents acting for their children, can register for the claim free of charge on the foundation’s website.
